wants.says: The visitor notices the budgeting app is relevant to their financial situation.
The visitor understands how the budgeting app can solve their financial problems.
The visitor believes the budgeting app can actually help them manage their finances better.
The visitor feels a sense of control over their financial future by using the budgeting app.
The visitor feels a sense of progress as they start using the budgeting app.
The visitor is open to purchasing the budgeting app.

lines.line: Create a section on the sales page where visitors can pick a named role that reflects their current financial situation.
For each section of the sales page, include a question that addresses a common financial concern or problem.
Include a statement on the sales page acknowledging uncertainties about financial management and how the app can help.
Provide a clear, step-by-step guide on the sales page for setting up and using the budgeting app for the first time.
Offer a free trial or demo of the budgeting app on the sales page to showcase its benefits before asking for a purchase.
Use imagery or a brief video on the sales page to set the context of the user's financial journey with the app.
Create a visual timeline on the sales page showing the user's progress in managing their finances with the app.
Write the sales page copy as if speaking to the user's younger self, highlighting the importance of financial planning.
Design the initial setup of the app to be intuitive and easy, ensuring the user can start using it within a minute.
Create a section on the sales page where visitors can pick a named role that reflects their current financial situation, followed by a series of questions addressing common financial concerns.
